title: Floral pigmentation as an embedded mechanistic demonstration of trait-history decomposition

role.dissertation_role: embedded depth test of the same Chapter 3 identifiability problem: after own ancestry and same-individual data localize a trait-state contrast, ask what biochemical, regulatory and selection-consistent genomic changes underlie that contrast
role.general_problem_bridge: P01-P05 provide the breadth test across Japanese Cirsium by asking where apparent species-tip transitions survive individual and population ancestry; M01 provides a depth test of what one retained trait-state contrast consists of biologically
role.core_independence: M01 is conceptually embedded in the Chapter 3 question, but failure, ambiguity or cancellation of M01 does not reorder, replace, validate or invalidate the locked P01-P05 core history-discrimination programme
role.not_primary_subject: Cirsium brevicaule and Cirsium irumtiense are the worked example, not the taxonomic subject of Chapter 3

literature_anchor.citation: Chang et al. 2026, BMC Plant Biology 26:545
accepted_premises: Cirsium brevicaule and Cirsium irumtiense are supported as distinct Ryukyu lineages/species separated across the Miyako Strait
the reported corolla contrast is white in C. brevicaule and bluish-purple in C. irumtiense
reported 2C genome sizes differ strongly, approximately 1.93 pg in C. brevicaule and 0.69 pg in C. irumtiense
not_estimands: basic species delimitation is not re-tested as the primary aim
matK rbcL trnL-F and ITS are not treated as sufficient to replace the published phylogenomic backbone
published lineage separation does not establish the ancestral floral pigment state, the molecular mechanism of the colour difference, selection on that mechanism or the identity of a selective agent

worked_example.primary_question: Can the observed floral-pigmentation contrast be decomposed into ancestral-state history, pigment chemistry, same-individual corolla expression and genomic evidence without presupposing loss or regain?

competing_histories.label: ancestral_pigment_loss
competing_histories.statement: the relevant ancestor was pigmented and the C. brevicaule lineage subsequently lost or strongly reduced floral anthocyanin pigmentation
competing_histories.support_rule: topology-robust ancestral-state inference supports a pigmented ancestor and a loss/reduction on the C. brevicaule side
competing_histories.falsifier: the admitted topology and trait ensemble does not support a pigmented ancestor or does not localize loss/reduction to the C. brevicaule side

competing_histories.label: ancestral_unpigmented_secondary_gain
competing_histories.statement: the relevant ancestor was unpigmented and the C. irumtiense lineage subsequently gained or regained floral anthocyanin pigmentation
competing_histories.support_rule: topology-robust ancestral-state inference supports an unpigmented ancestor and a gain on the C. irumtiense side
competing_histories.falsifier: the admitted topology and trait ensemble does not support an unpigmented ancestor or does not localize gain to the C. irumtiense side

competing_histories.label: simple_on_off_history_not_identified
competing_histories.statement: the data support neither a simple H1 nor H2 history because ancestral state, transition placement, pigment chemistry or reticulation remains ambiguous or indicates a more complex history
competing_histories.support_rule: H1 and H2 fail their predeclared support rules or multiple chemically or phylogenetically distinct transitions remain admissible
competing_histories.falsifier: one of H1 or H2 meets its frozen support rule across the admitted topology and trait ensemble

evidence_ladder.required_evidence: phenotypic contrast only or unresolved ancestral-state reconstruction
evidence_ladder.maximum_claim: a white versus bluish-purple contrast exists; no loss, regain, re-evolution or mechanistic claim

evidence_ladder.required_evidence: topology-robust ancestral-state inference plus homologous pigment chemistry across appropriately sampled focal and related taxa
evidence_ladder.maximum_claim: a loss, secondary gain or unresolved history may be identified; no molecular mechanism or selection claim

evidence_ladder.required_evidence: E1 plus same-individual corolla pigment chemistry and replicated corolla RNA-seq or independently validated expression for anthocyanin structural and regulatory genes
evidence_ladder.maximum_claim: a molecular-expression mechanism is associated with the trait transition; expression difference alone is not a causal regulatory variant, adaptation or selective-agent result

evidence_ladder.required_evidence: E2 plus orthology and mapping-bias qualification, replicated population genomic data, a frozen demographic/background-structure null and concordant support from multiple nonredundant selection statistics at a phenotype/expression-linked candidate region
evidence_ladder.maximum_claim: the candidate mechanism shows selection-consistent genomic evidence beyond the frozen background model; this is not proof of adaptation and does not identify pollinators or any other selective agent

evidence_ladder.required_evidence: E3 plus separately authorized direct functional perturbation and fitness evidence under a preregistered causal design
evidence_ladder.maximum_claim: only the causal molecular or fitness effect directly estimated by that experiment; selective-agent attribution still requires direct agent-specific ecological evidence

core_connection.stage_1_species_tip_contrast: the visible contrast is treated as a candidate trait-state difference, not yet a historical event
core_connection.stage_2_linked_history: individual/population ancestry and the admitted topology ensemble determine whether the contrast corresponds to a robust transition
core_connection.stage_3_transition_decomposition: pigment chemistry and same-individual expression determine what biological layer differs
core_connection.stage_4_selection_layer: population genomics tests whether the implicated mechanism departs from a frozen demographic/background expectation
core_connection.stage_5_causal_ecology: a separate functional or agent-specific ecological design is required to name fitness effects or a selective agent

mandatory_same_individual_fields: pigment-chemistry sample when destructive sampling is authorized
corolla RNA sample when authorized and developmentally matched
DNA sample and genomic library ID when authorized
sampling_contract.minimal_field_role: authorized collection of linked voucher or diagnostic images, leaf DNA material and developmentally matched floral material for pigment chemistry and RNA; manipulative pollination experiments are not required for M01 E0-E3
sampling_contract.selection_lane_population_requirement: population replication within each focal lineage is required; a two-species FST contrast alone is not admitted as evidence of selection

selection_contract.candidate_nomination: candidate regions must be linked prospectively to the pigment/expression mechanism or tested under a genome-wide procedure with frozen multiplicity control
selection_contract.background_null: neutral population structure and demographic history must be estimated before focal selection interpretation
selection_contract.mapping_and_orthology_gate: the strong reported genome-size difference requires explicit orthology, callable-region and mapping-bias checks before cross-lineage locus interpretation
selection_contract.minimum_evidence: multiple nonredundant statistics plus phenotype/expression concordance; any single outlier statistic is insufficient
prohibited_shortcuts: post-hoc threshold tuning after seeing candidate genes
treating absence of a sweep signature as evidence that historical selection did not occur
selection_contract.selective_agent_boundary: genomics alone cannot identify butterflies, flies, bees, climate or any other ecological factor as the selective agent

stop_rules: if ancestral state is not robust across the admitted topology and trait ensemble, stop loss/regain language at E0
if pigment chemistry is not homologously comparable, do not interpret visual colour as a single anthocyanin transition
if corolla RNA is not developmentally matched or biologically replicated, stop at chemistry and history
if orthology, callable regions or mapping bias cannot be qualified, do not run or interpret cross-lineage selection scans as selection evidence
if population replication or a demographic background model is absent, stop selection claims below E3
if only genomic evidence is available, do not name pollinators or another ecological factor as the causal selective agent
do not require M01 success for P01-P05 to remain valid
